questions.question: In which year did India win its first Hockey World Cup for Men's?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1975**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India won its first Hockey World Cup for Men's in 1975**, **defeating **arch-rivals **Pakistan **in the final held** in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia**.
 
• **1975 Men's Hockey World Cup**:
 
 
• The men's field hockey competition held annually at the Hockey World Cup was in its **third iteration in 1975**.
 
• **Malaysia's Kuala Lumpur** hosted the event.
 
• **India **won the match **against Pakistan** with a **2-1 **goal differential.
 
• **Ashok Kumar **scored the game-winning goal after **Surjit Singh** had scored the first important goal.
 
• For both countries, it was their second World Cup final participation; India finished second in the 1973 tournament while Pakistan won the first World Cup in 1971.
 
• For third place, Germany defeated the hosts, Malaysia, 4-0 on goal differential.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Men's Hockey World Cup:**

 
 
• The **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** is the organization that oversees the Men's FIH Hockey World Cup, an international field hockey championship.
 
• The competition **got underway in 1971**.
 
• Every four years, it serves as a bridge event between the Summer Olympics every four years.
 
• With four tournament victories, **Pakistan **is the **most successful** squad.
 
• Germany, Australia, and the Netherlands have each taken home three championships.
 
• The competition has been won once each by Belgium and India.
 
• The **2023 competition** took place in **Bhubaneswar, India**, between **January 13 and 29**.
 
• **Germany **won their **third World Cup title**, **defeating Belgium** 5–4 in a penalty shootout after the game finished in a 3–3 draw.
 
• In 2018, the World Cup was extended to sixteen teams.

questions.question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum wavelength?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **White light **is **split **into** seven colors** when passing through a triangular prism.
 
• The colors that are visible to the human eye are **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue**, **Indigo**, and **Violet**.
 
 
• These colors are commonly remembered using the acronym VIBGYOR.
 
• Typically, the human eye can detect **wavelengths from 380 to 700 nanometers**.
 
 
 
• **Violet **has the **minimum wavelength** among all, and it **deflects the most** when passed through a prism.
 
 
• Shorter wavelengths correspond to higher frequencies and higher energy in the visible spectrum.
 
 
 
• The** wavelength of the colour components** of white light:
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 **Colour**
 **Wavelength (in nanometers (nm))**
 
 

 Violet
 380-450
 
 

 Indigo
 450-480
 
 

 Blue
 480-500
 
 

 Green
 500-570
 
 

 Yellow
 570-590 
 
 

 Orange
 590-620
 
 

 Red
 620-750
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the 1660s, English physicist and mathematician Isaac Newton began a series of** experiments with sunlight and prisms**.

 
 
• He demonstrated that clear white light was composed of seven visible colors.
 
• One of the greatest scientific books ever written, Opticks, details Newton's findings from his experiments using prisms to bend light.
 
 
 
• The phenomenon of splitting light into its constituent colors is called dispersion.​
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as refraction.
 
 
• The bending caused by refraction allows us to create rainbows, prisms, magnifying glasses, and lenses.
 
• Our eyes are dependent on this light bending as well.

questions.question: Which of these regions received the first wave of the Green Revolution package?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first wave of the Green Revolution **package was received by more prosperous states of Haryana, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• 
 
The Green Revolution in India:

 
 
• The Green Revolution, which refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers.
 
• The Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965 under the Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).
 
• MS Swaminathan is considered the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• Norman Borlaug is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world.
 
• In India, the aim of this revolution was to increase the productivity of agricultural crops, particularly wheat and rice.
 
 
• The main focused crops were Wheat, Rice, Jowar, Bajra and Maize.
 
 
 
• In the first phase of the Green Revolution, the use of HYV seeds was limited to the more prosperous states of Haryana, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• HYV seeds refer to high-yielding varieties of seeds that were developed during the Green Revolution to increase crop yields.
 
 
• These are resistant to insects and diseases and have a high yield capacity.​
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution was a period of agricultural transformation that took place in the 1960s and 1970s in India.
 
• The goal of the Green Revolution was to increase agricultural productivity and food security by introducing high-yielding crop varieties (HYV seeds), modern irrigation systems, and chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• It was a significant success in India, as it helped to increase agricultural output (especially wheat and rice) and reduce food shortages.
 
• However, it also had some negative impacts, such as environmental degradation, soil erosion, and the loss of traditional farming practices.

questions.question: Which of the following initiatives of the Government of India is aimed at developing and rejuvenating 75 water bodies in each district of the country as a part of the celebration of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mission Amrit Sarovar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India initiated **Mission Amrit Sarovar**, aimed at **developing and rejuvenating 75 water bodies in each district **of the country, as a part of the celebration of **Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav**.
 
• The Prime Minister of India, Mr. **Modi**, has **launched it **on **April 24, 2022**.
 
• The mission is actively carried out by **eight Central ministries and departments**: the **Department of Rural Development**, the Department of Land Resources, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, the Department of Water Resources, the** Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, the Ministry of Forest, the Ministry of Environment and Climate Changes, the **Ministry of Railway**, and the **Ministry of Road, Transport & Highways**.
 
• It has enlisted the **Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Application and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N) **as a **technical partner**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav (AZAM):

 
 
• It is an initiative of the Government of India to celebrate and commemorate 75 years of independence and the glorious history of its people, culture and achievements. 
 
• It commenced on March 12, 2021, which started a 75-week countdown to our 75th anniversary of independence and ended on August 15, 2023.
 
• The Mahotsav is being celebrated on the basis of its 5 pillars:
 
 
• Struggle for independence,
 
• Ideas of 75 years,
 
• Achievements of 75 years,
 
• Actions of 75 years and
 
• Resolutions of 75 years.

questions.question: Which of these is a conventional weaker section lending under formal sector?

options.text: Self help group bank linkage model

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Commercial banks priority sector lending**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commercial banks priority sector lending (PSL)**:

 
 
• This refers to **mandatory lending requirements imposed by regulatory authorities** like the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI**) **on commercial banks**.
 
• These banks must allocate a specific portion of their **loans to specific categories considered "weaker sections," **including small and marginal farmers, micro and small enterprises, and weaker sections of society like **scheduled castes** and** scheduled tribes**.
 
• This makes it the most conventional and widespread form of formal sector lending reaching these groups.
 
• Rather of financing only successful industries or locations that are crucial to economic growth, the aim of a PSL project is to give credit to the less fortunate segments of society.
 
• Financial assistance is readily available to all key sectors, allowing them to apply for loans that banks are obligated to provide at a reduced interest rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money lenders**: Traditionally, money lenders operate outside the formal financial system, often charging high interest rates and lacking transparency.

 
 
• While they reach some weaker sections, they are not considered formal sector lending.
 
 
 
• **Self-help group (SHG) bank linkage model**: This model connects self-help groups formed by underprivileged individuals with banks, facilitating access to formal credit.
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs)**: Although MFIs cater to low-income populations, they are specialized institutions separate from the mainstream banking system.

questions.question: The net worth of any bank is equal to ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**assets (reserves + loans)** **- liabilities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To determine a **bank's net worth**, you **subtract its liabilities from its assets**.

 
 
• i.e. Total assets minus total liabilities.
 
 
 
• Assets: Everything the bank owns (loans, cash, investments, buildings, etc.)
 
• Liabilities: Everything the bank owes (customer deposits, loans payable, etc.)
 
• Net worth: The difference between assets and liabilities (what the bank truly owns after accounting for all its debts)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India’s central bank.

 
 
• In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, it was founded on April 1, 1935 in Calcutta.

 
 
• It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
 
 
• Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• As a qualitative instrument of monetary policy, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) employs moral suasion.
 
• It regulates the issue of Bank notes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

questions.question: Who among the following personalities coined the term 'Odissi' for Odisha's classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabichandra Kalicharan Patnaik**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Odisha's classical dance style was named "Odissi" by** Oriya poet, dramatist, and researcher **Kavichandra Kalicharan Pattanayak**.
 
• **Kavichandra Kalicharan Pattanayak**:
 
 
• He, was often called **Kabichandra**, was a renowned **Odishan writer and artist**.
 
• He made contributions to the fields of Odissi theater, dance, and music.
 
• Additionally, he made a substantial contribution to the early development of the Odia film.
 
• On **December 23, 1898**, he was **born **in **Badamba**, a princely kingdom at the time.
 
• The **Odissi music and dance community** frequently performs his pieces in a variety of traditional ragas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy:

 
 
• ​In Radhanagar, Bengal, on May 22, 1772, Raja Ram Mohan Roy was born into an orthodox Brahman household.
 
• He is regarded as the "Father of Modern India" and ‘Father of Indian Renaissance’.
 
• In Patna, he studied Persian and Arabic in his early schooling. There, he read the Quran, the writings of Sufi mystic poets, and the Arabic translations of Plato and Aristotle.
 
• He read the Vedas and Upnishads and studied Sanskrit in Benaras.
 
• When he was sixteen, he penned a logical criticism of Hindu idolatry after returning to his village.
 
• He served as Woodforde's and Digby's personal diwan for the East India Company from 1803 until 1814.
 
• He left his position in 1814 and relocated to Calcutta to dedicate his life to religious, social, and political reforms.
 
• He founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1815, the Calcutta Unitarian Association in 1821, and the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 which later became the Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore:
 
 
• Bengali polymath Rabindranath Tagore (7 May 1861 – 7 August 1941) was involved in the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He was a poet, novelist, playwright, composer, philosopher, social reformer, educator, and painter.
 
• Using Contextual Modernism in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, he transformed Indian art and music as well as Bengali literature.
 
• In 1913, he became the first non-European and the first lyricist to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in recognition of his work Geetanjali.
 
• In the 1915, King George V bestowed upon Tagore a knighthood, which he later renounced following the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• While Tagore's graceful prose and enchanted poetry were immensely well-liked throughout the Indian subcontinent, his poetic songs were perceived as mystical and mercurial.
 
• He was a fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society.
 
• Tagore was referred as "the Bard of Bengal" and went by the monikers Gurudeb, Kobiguru, and Biswokobi.
 
• Geetanjali, Sadhana, Ghare-Baire, Gora and Rabindra Sangeet are among his important works.
 
• His works, "Jana Gana Mana" in India and "Amar Shonar Bangla" in Bangladesh, were selected as national anthems by two countries. West Bengal has made "Banglar Mati Banglar Jol" into its official state anthem.
 
• In 1901 he founded the famous Shantiniketan which later came to be known as Vishwabharati University.

questions.question: Deepavali is celebrated in which month of Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kartika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kartik (October-November):

 
 
• The Hindu calendar's eighth month, Kartik, is linked to the celebration of Deepavali (Diwali), the festival of lights.
 
• The month is also linked to the observance of Karva Chauth, a festival honoring the marriage union of husband and wife.
 
• It is also linked with festival of Bhai Dooj.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chaitra (March-April): 

 
 
• In the Hindu calendar, the first month is Chaitra and is highly fortunate.
 
• Occurs in March or April on the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The Hindu New Year, known in Maharashtra as Gudi Padwa, in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana as Ugadi, and in other parts of India as Chaitra Navratri, ushers in the month.
 
• The month is linked to fresh starts, development, and wealth as well as the start of the spring season.
 
 

 
• Ashwin (September-October): 

 
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, Ashwin, the seventh month, is connected to the celebration of Navratri, a holiday honoring the divine feminine force.
 
• Additionally, the month is linked to the celebration of Dussehra, a festival honoring Lord Rama's victory over the demon king Ravana.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2011, which state in India has the highest population density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bihar__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **highest population density (person per square kilometre)**, as per the 2011 Census, is in **Bihar**, with **1106**
 
• The **population density **of **West Bengal** is **1028**, **Kerala **is **860**, and **Uttar Pradesh** is **829**.
 
• The overall population density of India is **382**.
 
• Census of India 2011:
 
 
• It started on April 1, 2010.
 
• "Our Census, Our Future" was the 2011 census's slogan.
 
• India's population, according to the 2011 Census, is estimated to be 1.21 billion.
 
• The population density was 382 persons per square kilometer in 2011.
 
• India's sex ratio, as per the 2011 census, is 940.
 
• India's child sex ratio is 918, the lowest since the country's independence, as per Census 2011.
 
• This marked the commencement of the 15th Census of India and the 7th Census of Independent India (2011).
 
• The Indian Census Commissioner for 2011 was C. Chandramouli.
 
• The 2011 India Census was carried out in two phases:
 
 
• House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010).
 
• Population Enumeration (9th to 28 February 2011).
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population density** is the **number of people per unit of area**, usually transcribed as "**per square kilometer**" or square mile.
 
• The 1948 Census Act governs how the census is carried out.
 
 
• The Indian Home Minister at the time, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, spearheaded the bill for this Act.
 
• The Indian Constitution's Article 246 declares the population census to be a Union subject.
 
• It is mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution under serial number 69.
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs' Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner oversees the decennial census.
 
 
 
• The first census of India was conducted by Lord Mayo in 1872.
 
• The first official census was started by Lord Ripon in 1881.

questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is NOT borrowed from the Canadian constitution?

options.text: Appointment of state governor by the centre

__
 
• **India's Constitution** establishes a crucial framework that defines the nature of the political system, the authorities' responsibilities, and the people's basic rights and obligations to the nation.
 
• The** protection of peoples' fundamental rights **is the primary goal of the constitution.
 
• The Indian Constituent Assembly **enacted **the constitution on **November 26, 1949** and **became operative on January 26, 1950**. 
 
• Some features of Indian constitution were borrowed from constitutions of different countries of the world.
 
 
• Important **provisions adopted** from the Constitution of **Canada**:
 
 
• Centrifugal form of federalism where the centre is stronger than the states.
 
• Residuary powers vest with the centre
 
• Centre appoints the Governors at the states
 
• Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court .
 
 
 
• **Concurrent list** was adopted **from Australia**n Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a kind of Xanthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Microbial gum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xanthan gum** is a **microbial gum produced by **the **bacterium *Xanthomonas campestris***.

 
 
• This polysaccharide finds **numerous industrial applications**, one of which is as a **prevalent food additive**.
 
• It works well as **a stabilizer **and thickening agent to keep ingredients from separating.
 
• It can be **made through fermentation from simple sugars** or carbohydrates.
 
• It was first **identified by **US Department of Agriculture researcher **Allene Rosalind Jeanes** and her team, and in the early **1960s**, **CP Kelco** **commercialized **it under the brand **name Kelzan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seed gum**: This type of gum is extracted from the seeds of various plants like guar beans and locust beans.

 
 
• Examples include **guar gum** and** tara gum**.
 
 
 
• **Seaweed gum**: This type of gum is extracted from different types of seaweeds.
 
 
• Examples include **agar-agar**, **alginate**, and **carrageenan**.
 
 
 
• **Exudate gum**: This type of gum is naturally exuded from trees and other plants as a protective measure.
 
 
• Examples include **gum arabic** and **gum tragacanth**.

questions.question: The Muhammedan Literary Society founded in Calcutta in 1863 was founded by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nawab Abdul Latif**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammedan Literary Society**:

 
 
• Muslim writers in British India formed the** Mohammedan Literary Society**.
 
• It was founded **in Calcutta in 1863** by **Nawab Abdul Latif**, and the **Muslim Institute of Calcutta** took its place in **1930**.
 
• **Latif **served as the society's **secretary**, and Mysore's Prince **Mahomed Ruheemoodin** served as **president**.
 
• 
 
• The society used Arabic, English, Persian, and Urdu languages.
 
 
 
• **Nawab Bahadur Qazi Abdul Latif**:
 
 
• He was a social worker, professor, and nobleman of Bengali Muslim descent.
 
• In **1880**, the **British bestowed** upon him the **title Nawab**.
 
• He was among the first Muslims in India during the 1800s to accept modernity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan**:

 
 
• He was born into a wealthy, aristocratic family with intimate ties to the Mughal court in Delhi, the capital of the Mughal Empire.
 
• He received instruction in both science and the Quran.
 
• In his insightful pamphlet **"Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind"** (Reasons for the Indian Revolt of 1857), he identified the main causes of the uprising as British ignorance and aggressive expansionist policies.
 
• He supported interfaith harmony as well. In addition, he wrote a book titled **"Commentary on the Holy Bible"** and was a Christian scholar.
 
• In order to further education, he **founded **a number of educational institutions, the most notable of which was the** Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College (MAOC)**, founded in **1875**.
 
 
• It subsequently evolved into the **Aligarh Muslim University**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Mirza Ghulam Ahmad**:
 
 
• The **Ahmadiyya Movement**, which he founded, got its start **in Punjab**, British India, in **1889**.
 
• It was a movement of modern messianism.
 
• It was established on liberal ideas, the belief that religion should be accessible to all people, opposition to jihad, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following states is the largest producer of jowar in India, as of 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharastra.**__

__
 
• **Maharastra is the top producer of jowar in India.**
 
• **Jowar:**
 
 
• It is a crop that is mostly grown in moist areas and is rainfed; irrigation is rarely necessary.
 
• In terms of both production and area, it ranks as the** third-most significant food crop.**
 
• **Rainfall: 30-100 cm of moderate rain**.
 
• **Temperatures: high temperatures ranging from 20 to 32°C.**
 
• Vulnerability of Jowar: Both excessive moisture and prolonged drought are harmful.
 
• **Soil: Light soils with good drainage are ideal.**
 
• It is cultivated as the major food crop in semi-arid areas of central and south India.
 
• In north India, Jowar is mainly a** Kharif crop** whereas it is **sown as both Kharif and Rabi in the southern states.**
 
• **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh are the top producers.**
 
• **India is the largest producer of jowar in the world.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of vegetation found in the Himalayan region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alpine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alpine **is a type of vegetation found in the **Himalayan region**.
 
• **Alpine**:
 
 
• This type of vegetation is characterized by **low-growing plants**, **grasses**, mosses, and **lichens adapted to harsh cold and windy conditions** at high altitudes.
 
• The **Himalayas**, being a vast mountain range, have **extensive alpine zones** with diverse flora perfectly suited to this environment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mangrove**: These are **salt-tolerant trees and shrubs** found in** coastal areas** and **tidal wetlands**, mainly in tropical and **subtropical regions**. The Himalayas are far from the coast and lack the necessary conditions for mangroves to thrive.
 
• **Pampas**: These are** tall grasses **native to **South America**, primarily **Argentina **and **Uruguay**.
 
• **Savannah**: These are **grasslands** with scattered trees and shrubs, typically found in **Africa**.

questions.question: Who among the following won the gold medal in the girls' under 15 category at the Asian Juniors Individual Squash Championship in June 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anahat Singh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anahat Singh:**

 
 
• She is an **Indian squash player** who was born on March 13, 2008.
 
• She was the **youngest athlete to represent India at the 2022 Commonwealth Games**, having turned 14 years old.
 
• She took home the** Asian Junior Squash Individual Championships Girls U15 championship in June 2022.**
 
• She emerged **victorious at the August 2023 Asian Junior Squash Individual Championships in Dalian, China, winning the Girls U17 division.**
 
• Subsequently,** she won two bronze medals** in the women's team event and mixed doubles alongside Abhay Singh **in Asian Games, 2022.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Squash:**

 
 
• It is a** racquet and ball sports, **but squash's dynamics are very different from other racquet and ball sports like tennis etc.
 
• It was **created in England** in the **early 1800s** and has quickly become well-liked by players of all skill levels.
 
• It is a **part of the Asian Games since 1986 and the Commonwealth Games since 1998**, although** not yet being an Olympic sport.**
 
• Since the mid-1970s, there have also been high-profile, specialised competitions such as the World Squash Championships.
 
 
 
• Asians Games:
 
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from across Asia.
 
• They were regulated by the Asian Games Federation (AGF) till 1978.
 
• The first games were in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
 
• Since the breakup of the Asian Games Federation in 1982, the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) has organized the Games.
 
• The Games are recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and are described as the second largest multi-sport event after the Olympic Games.
 
• The next edition is expected to be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan in 2026.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan Kumari Kamala is associated with which Indian dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumari Kamala** was an exceptional Indian classical **Kathak dancer **who was born on June 16th, 1934.

 
 
• She made appearances in over 100 Tamil, Kannada, Telegu, and Hindi films as a kid dancer.
 
• With the **aid of Shankar Rao Vyas**, she became well-versed in Hindustani classical music, and **Lachhu Maharaj in Bombay trained her in Kathak.**
 
• With **"Nam Iruvar," her film**, she achieved great success.
 
• She starred in the **lead role of "Jagathalaprathapan," a Tamil film**.
 
• She was asked to play for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation celebrations in 1953, and during the 1950s, she went on tour through China and Japan.
 
• Even after receiving the **Branta Professorship in 1975**, she attended Colgate University for two terms.
 
• In **1970**, she received the **Padma Bhushan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kathak:

 
 
• The well-known ancient Indian classical dance known as Kathak is said to have originated with the nomadic storytellers from North India known as Kathakars.
 
• These Kathakars traveled and told tales using songs, dances, and music that were reminiscent of classical Greek theatre.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text written by Bharata Muni.
 
• The three chief sections of a Kathak dance are:
 
 
• Invocation: The act of an artist offering a prayer or salutation to God and their guru is known as an invocation.
 
 
• Hindu performers employ mudras, or hand gestures, to convey the same message.
 
• On Muslim holidays, the artist presents a "salami."
 
 
 
• Nritta: The artist's portrayal of pure dancing.
 
 
• He or she begins by moving the neck, wrists, and eyebrows slowly and elegantly.
 
• The quick sequences according to "bols" come next. A bol is a brief rhythmic pattern sequence. Here, the artist also demonstrates lively footwork.
 
 
 
• Nritya: In this piece, the performer uses facial expressions, slow body motions, and vocal and instrumental music to tell a tale or explore a theme.

questions.question: SRD Prasad received the Padma Shri in 2023, for his contribution to the sport of ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalaripayattu.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SRD Prasad:**

 
 
• **Padma Shri 2023** has been given to **Kerala's Kalaripayattu Acharya SRD Prasad** in recognition of his services to sports.
 
• The martial technique that SRD Prasad Gurukkal learned from** his father, Chirakkal T. Sreedharan Nair,** a legendary figure in Kalaripayattu, has been a lifelong study and teaching endeavour for him.
 
• Respected and experienced in the world of kalarippayattu, Prasad is also a skilled author and orator with mastery over the martial artform.
 
• He is the **recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademy award.**
 
• He** operates the well-known SRD Prasad Gurukul **to educate interested parties about the specialised art form.
 
 
 
• **Kalaripayattu**:
 
 
• The words **"Kalari" (meaning gym or training area) and "payattu" (meaning to battle or exercise)** are the origin of the phrase Kalaripayattu.
 
• **Kerala** is where Kalaripayattu, one of the **world's oldest and most scientific martial arts**, originated.
 
• Praised as Kerala's pride, it enjoys international recognition and esteem.
 
• The first step of the training is to massage the body with oil until it is supple and agile.
 
• Other essential elements of the **art form are feats like marichil (somersault), ottam (running), and chattom (jumping).**
 
• Additionally, there are instruction in the** use of weapons such as maces, swords, daggers, spears, and bows and arrows. **
 
• The ultimate goal is complete mental-body synergy. Kalaripayattu also emphasises specialising in traditional medical methods. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Padma Shri:

 
 
• The Padma Shri, which is also written Padma Shree, is the fourth-highest civilian honor granted by the Indian Republic, ranking behind the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, and Padma Bhushan.
 
• Awardees are chosen for their "distinguished contribution in various spheres of activity including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, acting, medicine, social service and public affairs."
 
• The award was established on January 2, 1954.
 
• Every year on India's Republic Day, the Indian government bestows this honour.

questions.question: In India, ___________ fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is an important tool used by the RBI to manage liquidity in the banking system and control inflation.
 
• Cash reserve ratio (CRR): 
 
 
• It is a monetary policy tool used by central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), to regulate and control the money supply in the economy.
 
• CRR is the percentage of total deposits that commercial banks are required to keep as reserves with the central bank.
 
• It is a portion of the bank's demand and time liabilities.
 
• The primary objective of implementing CRR is to ensure the liquidity and stability of the banking system while controlling inflation and managing credit growth.
 
• When the central bank increases the CRR, it reduces the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks.
 
• This helps reduce excess liquidity in the economy by controlling inflationary pressures and curbing excessive credit expansion.
 
• On the other hand, **when **the **central bank decreases the CRR**, **it increases the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks**.
 
• This can stimulate credit growth, promote economic activity, and ease liquidity conditions in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reserve Bank of India (RBI):

 
 
• It is **India’s central bank**.
 
• In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, it was founded on April 1, 1935 in Calcutta.
 
• It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• It also functions as the "lender of last resort" and is considered Banker to Banks.
 
• It regulates the issue of Bank notes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).
